name: persoonsnummer
note: Curaçao's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: a TIN (in Dutch the persoonsnummer) is allocated by the Tax Department to a person who requests it, one for every tax; not automatically at birth or at an age, nor to someone not taxable; the automated system generates 9 digits after registering the person's details. Read as given on application, to anyone. No check rule, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Curaçao: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: A TIN (in Dutch called “persoonsnummer”) is allocated to a natural person or entity if the person or entity requests this at the Tax Department. ... When child is born When child reaches a certain age. When person is not classified as taxable ... The TIN is generated by the automated system after registering certain data of a tax payer and exists of 9 digits.
